gaps.sentence: The thunderstorm was absolutely ___ , so the children hid under the blankets (TERRIFY).
gaps.hint: the storm causes the fear (-ing); note 'terrific' means excellent
gaps.explanation: The storm causes terror, so it is terrifying; the children felt terrified. 'Terrific' means excellent.

gaps.sentence: She was ___ to accept the conditions at first (WILLING).
gaps.hint: negative adjective needed: she did not want to
gaps.explanation: 'At first' suggests reluctance, so the negative adjective 'unwilling' (un- + willing) is needed.

gaps.sentence: The government's ___ (DECIDE) to raise taxes was criticized.
gaps.explanation: After 'The government's' a noun is needed: decision (-sion noun); 'decisive' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: Don't ___ your children — let them make their own mistakes (PROTECT).
gaps.hint: protect too much (over-); a base verb is needed
gaps.explanation: The prefix over- means excessively: overprotect means to protect too much. A base verb follows 'Don't'.

gaps.sentence: We ___ the cost of the trip and ran out of money (ESTIMATE).
gaps.hint: judged it too low — that is why the money ran out (under-)
gaps.explanation: Running out of money shows the estimate was too low: underestimated (under- + estimated).

gaps.sentence: The soup tastes a bit ___ ; add some salt (TASTE).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -less means without: tasteless explains why salt is needed. An adjective follows 'tastes'.

gaps.sentence: The train arrived ___ , despite the snow (PUNCTUAL).
gaps.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify 'arrived': punctually (-ly). 'Punctuality' is the noun.
